title: Zoom in: how a Sentinel failover replaces a dead primary
caption: Sentinels agree the primary is down, promote one replica and hand clients the new address; anything not yet replicated is lost.

messages.label: replicate
messages.note: Replication is asynchronous: the primary has already answered the client.

messages.label: PING
messages.note: The primary's machine dies. Each Sentinel stops getting replies.

messages.label: agree: primary down
messages.note: After the timeout, a quorum (2 of 3) must agree before anything happens, so one Sentinel's network blip can't trigger a failover.

messages.label: REPLICAOF NO ONE
messages.note: The most up-to-date replica is promoted.

messages.label: where is the primary?
messages.note: Sentinel-aware clients ask on reconnect, or get a switch notification.

messages.label: ZINCRBY board 30 p8
messages.note: Writes resume after roughly 10–30 s in total.

scenarios.name: Lost writes
scenarios.summary: A write acknowledged just before the crash never reached the replica. After failover it is simply gone.

messages.label: replicate
messages.note: The primary dies before the stream reaches the replica.

messages.label: HGETALL session:abc
messages.note: The new primary has never heard of this session: the player logs in again.

scenarios.name: Stale client address
scenarios.summary: A client that cached the old address keeps talking to the old node after it comes back as a replica.

messages.label: REPLICAOF new primary
messages.note: The old primary restarts and is turned into a replica.

messages.label: ZINCRBY board 10 p3
messages.note: This client never re-asked the Sentinels.

messages.label: where is the primary?
messages.note: Fix: on READONLY or a connection error, ask the Sentinels again and retry.

scenarios.name: Alternative: Redis Cluster
scenarios.summary: No Sentinels: the other primaries of the cluster detect the failure and vote. Same async-replication trade-off, but data is also sharded over slots.

messages.label: gossip ping
messages.note: Primary A stops answering the cluster bus.

messages.label: vote for me
messages.note: A's replica asks the other primaries for votes and takes over A's slots.

messages.label: GET {u7}:rank
messages.note: The client still thinks A owns this slot.

messages.label: GET {u7}:rank
messages.note: Cluster clients refresh their slot map on MOVED.
